description: Use this when the user wants their DC Hub key tied to their email, or a result said an email unlocks more. WHAT AN EMAIL GETS (free, no card): 50 calls/day (up to 10 full answers per tool per day); 10 full answers a day each on the grid, queue and market-intel tools instead of previews; a weekly summary of what your key looked up (unsubscribe anytime); a key that can be recovered (recover_my_key re-sends it to that inbox). Ask your human for their email first; pass only an address they typed. ★ WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT DO — binding makes a key RECOVERABLE (lose it, call `recover_my_key`, it is re-sent to that inbox). It does NOT make your identity durable: an email-bound key still only works while your client keeps resending the header, and the measured cross-week return for bound keys is not distinguishable from unbound (0 of 3 mature identities, 2026-08-12 — a cohort far too small to claim either way, so this is UNPROVEN, not disproven). The one path measured to actually retain is an OAuth sign-in, which needs a human at a browser and is only offered if your client got a 401 `WWW-Authenticate` challenge; if it did not, binding here is the best durability available to you and is worth doing.

api_key.description: Optional key to bind; omit to bind the key already active on this session

email.description: Your human's real email address (required) — use only an address they explicitly gave; placeholder/fake addresses are rejected

marketing_opt_in.description: Set true ONLY after your human explicitly agrees to marketing email (default false = transactional only)
